definitions.explanation: Pepper as a seasoning, especially black or white pepper. Loanword from English; appears mostly in cooking product names and compounds, while {胡椒|こしょう} is the everyday word.

examples.japanese: ペッパーを{加|くわ}える。
ブラックペッパーを{挽|ひ}いてかける。
examples.english: Grind some black pepper and sprinkle it on.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}とペッパーだけのシンプルな{味付|あじつ}けが、{素材|そざい}のよさを{引|ひ}き{立|た}たせる。
examples.english: A simple seasoning of just salt and pepper brings out the quality of the ingredients.

notes:
ペッパー sounds more modern/Western than {胡椒|こしょう} and is favored in product names, restaurant menus, and recipes with a Western feel. In daily speech, most cooks still say {胡椒|こしょう}.

COMPOUNDS:
- ブラックペッパー: black pepper
- ホワイトペッパー: white pepper
- レモンペッパー: lemon pepper
- ペッパーミル: pepper mill

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {胡椒|こしょう}: pepper — the everyday word in Japanese
- {唐辛子|とうがらし}: chili pepper — unrelated; a separate spice
- スパイス: spices — broad category that includes pepper
